Article Title: 'No satisfaction unless I play for India': Gurjapneet Singh after four-wicket haul against Uttarakhand
Article Text:
Tamil Nadu's Gurjapneet Singh bowls on the first day of a Ranji Trophy cricket match between Tamil Nadu and Uttarakhand, in Chennai. (PTI Photo)

Gurjapneet makes early inroads with the new ball

Managing workload after India A stint

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Bowling to India's stars boosts confidence

For Gurjapneet Singh, a strong performance in domestic cricket is only another step towards a bigger goal. The Tamil Nadu left-arm pacer made an immediate impact against Uttarakhand in the Ranji Trophy , claiming four wickets on the opening day, but insisted that his job would remain unfinished until he earns a chance to represent India.Playing just his 10th first-class match, Gurjapneet returned figures of 4/34 as Tamil Nadu bowled out Uttarakhand, last season’s semi-finalists, for 134 in their Elite Group D clash at the MA Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai.“There is no satisfaction unless I play for India. That's the main job, and that box is still empty. I have to tick that,” Gurjapneet told reporters at the end of the first day's play.The 26-year-old, who represents Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in the IPL and is part of the BCCI's targeted pool of fast bowlers, missed Tamil Nadu's previous match against Rajasthan in Jaipur while representing India A in the 50-over series against Australia in Puducherry.Operating with the new ball on a red-soil surface affected by heavy overnight rain, Gurjapneet struck early to put Uttarakhand on the back foot. He dismissed Aarav Mahajan before trapping Dega Nischal leg-before-wicket and removing Kunal Chandela during an incisive opening spell. He also troubled India Under-19 batter Lakshya Raichandani before returning to dismiss Uttarakhand's top-scorer, Avneesh Sudha, for 54 and complete his four-wicket haul.Gurjapneet attributed his success to reading the batters and adjusting his angles rather than sticking to a fixed plan.“It is just instinct. I watch his feet movement and how he is reacting. One ball I bowl from over the stumps and later I come around the stumps. Maybe his conscious mind is ready to play from that angle, and the results were positive,” he explained.Having battled injuries in the past, Gurjapneet has also focused on preparing his body for the demands of red-ball cricket after switching from the shorter format.“I was practising a lot with both balls. Coming into the Ranji Trophy, the workload is high and you have to keep maintaining that,” he said.He added that managing his fitness and energy levels was crucial to bowling long spells without overexerting himself.“I'm just trying to keep that energy the same because I know in red-ball cricket, it's difficult to bowl long spells. I'm trying to keep my body ready for all spells and deliver that.”Gurjapneet's experience as a net bowler with the Indian team has helped strengthen his belief in his abilities. Bowling to established international batters such as Shubman Gill and Virat Kohli , he said, gave him confidence that he could carry into domestic cricket.He has also benefited from conversations with India bowling coach Morne Morkel , who advised him to focus on his lengths and keep varying his angles.“He just said you have good skills and to keep focusing on your length and keep changing angles,” Gurjapneet recalled.
Article Summary: Gurjapneet Singh takes four wickets as Tamil Nadu beat Uttarakhand. The 26-year- old is part of the BCCI's targeted pool of fast bowlers. He missed Tamil Nadu's previous match against Rajasthan while representing India A in the 50-over series against Australia.

Article Title: Shafali Verma scripts history with ninth 50-plus score as India thrash Zimbabwe to seal T20I series
Article Text:
Shafali Verma scripts history (Image: BCCI/X)

India’s bowlers restrict Zimbabwe to 102/8

Shafali Verma continued her prolific run in women’s T20 internationals, smashing a 25-ball 55 as India thrashed Zimbabwe by nine wickets in the second T20I to take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series on Sunday.The Indian opener set a new benchmark for the most 50-plus scores by a batter in a calendar year in women’s T20Is, registering her ninth such innings in 2026. She moved past Smriti Mandhana , who recorded eight 50-plus scores in 2024, while Mithali Raj and Hong Kong’s Natasha Miles have seven and eight, respectively, in 2018 and 2026.Shafali’s latest half-century, her 22nd in T20Is, came as India chased down Zimbabwe’s modest target of 103 in just 8.5 overs after restricting the visitors to 102/8.Shafali and captain Smriti Mandhana combined to make short work of the chase, sharing a 96-run opening partnership that put India firmly in control. Mandhana remained unbeaten on 47, while Shafali’s aggressive knock featured sixes and boundaries that left Zimbabwe’s bowlers struggling for answers.The stand also extended the pair’s remarkable record in 2026. Shafali and Mandhana have now registered nine 50-plus partnerships in women’s T20Is this calendar year, the most by any pair.They surpassed their own tally of seven such stands in 2024 and moved ahead of Hong Kong’s Yasmin Daswani and Natasha Miles, who have eight in 2026.Shafali reached her half-century in 26 balls, taking on off-spinner Beloved Biza for a six. She also punished Michelle Mavunga with three consecutive deliveries yielding four, four and six. Mandhana, meanwhile, struck four successive boundaries against pacer Nyasha Gwanzura before finishing the chase with an inside-out six off Olinder Chare.The victory also gave Mandhana a series win at the start of her full-time captaincy stint.Earlier, India’s bowlers delivered a disciplined performance to prevent Zimbabwe from building momentum after the visitors opted to bat first. Nandani Sharma dismissed opener Kelis Ndhlovu for a duck, and Zimbabwe managed only 20 runs in the powerplay. Beloved Biza departed soon after, leaving the visitors under pressure.Chipo Tiripano top-scored with 34 off 32 balls, while captain Josephine Nkomo remained unbeaten on 27. The pair added 45 runs for the fourth wicket, providing Zimbabwe with their most productive phase of the innings.However, off-spinner Niki Prasad broke the stand by having Tiripano caught behind by wicketkeeper Richa Ghosh. Prasad later trapped Nyasha Gwanzura leg-before to finish with figures of 2/7 and leave Zimbabwe restricted to 102/8.India’s commanding chase, powered by Shafali’s record-setting half-century and her prolific partnership with Mandhana, ensured the hosts secured the series with one match remaining.
Article Summary: Shafali Verma hits 55 as India beat Zimbabwe by nine wickets in second T20I. Indian opener sets new benchmark for most 50-plus scores by a batter in a calendar year in women's T20Is. Shafali and captain Smriti Mandhana have now registered nine 50- plus partnerships in women’s T20is this calendar year.

Article Title: Ranji Trophy: Tushar Deshpande rocks Himachal as Mumbai take control, close in on first-innings lead

Tushar Despande

Deshpande's four-wicket haul puts Mumbai in control

The opening day of the Ranji Trophy witnessed impressive bowling performances from Mumbai pacer Tushar Deshpande who claimed four wickets to put their Mumbai in commanding positions. Mumbai bowled out Himachal Pradesh for 140 and finished the day just 33 runs short of taking the first-innings lead.Mumbai closed in on a first-innings lead against Himachal Pradesh after Deshpande's four-wicket haul helped dismiss the hosts for 140 in 39.5 overs in their Ranji Trophy Group D encounter in Bilaspur on Sunday.Deshpande returned figures of 4/46, making the most of the early conditions to trouble the Himachal batters with disciplined bowling. Mumbai reached 107/2 in 36 overs at stumps, requiring just 33 more runs to take the lead with eight wickets remaining.The Mumbai pacer made an immediate impact, dismissing opener Shubham Arora for a duck with the first ball of the match. He then trapped Nehal Wadhera lbw for eight in the third over as Himachal slipped to 22/3 inside the first six overs. However, Musheer Khan (34 not out) and captain Siddhesh Lad (32 not out) steadied the innings with an unbeaten 75-run partnership for the third wicket.Deshpande, playing his 51st first-class match, is also closing in on the milestone of 150 wickets in the format.

Rizwan Returns After Lengthy Absence From Competitive Cricket

Pakistan wicketkeeper-batter Mohammad Rizwan has been cleared to return to domestic cricket amid an ongoing inquiry into allegations involving online betting, gambling and the leaking of dressing-room information. The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) has permitted him to feature in the ongoing Presidents Cup first-class tournament, offering the veteran batter a reprieve as the investigation continues.Former Pakistan captain Mohammad Hafeez, who serves as director and head coach of Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited (SNGPL), confirmed that he had received an email from the PCB's domestic department authorising Rizwan to play from October 19.The fifth round of the tournament began on Monday, with Rizwan expected to captain the SNGPL side, Hafeez said.Rizwan and fellow Pakistan batter Imam-ul-Haq were barred from domestic cricket after being called back from England following the second Test in August. Both players were asked to face an inquiry by the National Cyber Crime Cell (NCCA) over alleged leaks of dressing-room information and issues related to online betting and gambling.Rizwan has appeared before the agency twice for questioning. However, the exact nature of the complaints being investigated by the government body remains unclear.The phones belonging to Rizwan and Imam were also seized by security personnel accompanying the Pakistan team during the second Test at Lord's. The devices remain with the NCCA for forensic examination as part of the inquiry.While Imam has largely remained out of the public eye, Rizwan has continued to attract attention amid the investigation. However, a reliable source indicated on Sunday that the situation had largely eased following the wicketkeeper-batter's most recent session with the NCCA on October 10 in Lahore.The source also suggested that the inquiry could be concluded soon, although no official announcement confirming its closure has been made.The PCB's decision to allow Rizwan to resume domestic cricket marks a significant development in the matter. However, permission to play should not be interpreted as confirmation that the inquiry has been concluded or that the allegations have been resolved.Rizwan, who has represented Pakistan in 47 Tests, 103 ODIs and 106 T20 Internationals, has not played competitive cricket since the second Test against England at Lord's.
Article Summary: Pakistan wicketkeeper-batter Mohammad Rizwan has been cleared to return to domestic cricket amid an ongoing inquiry. Article Title: From selling vegetables to Commonwealth medal: Now Jhandu Kumar dreams of Asian Para Games glory
Article Text:
Jhandu Kumar

Kolkata:

TOI

Not too long ago, Jhandu Kumar used to sell vegetables and drive an e-rickshaw to meet his own expenses and help run the family household. Today, the Bihar para-powerlifter is a Commonwealth Games bronze medallist, has secured a government job and is preparing to represent India at Asian Para Games.For Jhandu, who finished on the podium in the men’s heavyweight para-powerlifting event at the 2026 Commonwealth Games with a 190kg lift, the transformation still feels like a dream.“Yes, absolutely. It feels like a dream. A boy from a village who worked hard is now making a name for himself across the country,” Jhandu toldfrom Aichi-Nagoya. “I cannot express how happy I am. Words fail me. Now I have another opportunity at the Asian Para Games to represent my country.”The athlete from Harnaut village in Bihar’s Nalanda district will compete in the 72kg category on Tuesday. He continued his training for the Games at the National Centre of Excellence in Gandhinagar under coach Rajinder Singh Rahelu. More than making drastic changes to his training, he concentrated on strengthening the self-belief that has driven his rise.“The basic approach remains the same. For me, it is about maintaining that inner drive and staying motivated.I have this determination within me: ‘I will do it, I will definitely succeed,’” said the 29-year-old. “That has been my main focus, to perform even better.”However, Jhandu knows there will be little margin for error in a competitive field. Asked what sort of lift could put him in medal contention, he said the numbers alone would not determine the outcome.“A medal could come at 200kg, 205kg or even 190kg. During competition, the mind works differently. You have to manage everything, and there is pressure,” he said. “You have to handle that pressure, and then it depends on how your body responds and how much you can push yourself.”Irrespective of the numbers, Jhandu expects stiff competition and is relishing the challenge. “There are many strong competitors. Lifter from China and Malaysia will be among them, apart from athletes from several other countries. Competition is inevitable. In fact, without competition, it would not be exciting,” Jhandu said.Despite all that he has achieved, Jhandu admits his journey still feels surreal. “Honestly, I never imagined that I would one day compete at Commonwealth Games or Asian Para Games. My focus was simply on working hard and winning a medal for my country,” he said.That hard work has paid off, and the medal in Glasgow did more than establish Jhandu on the international stage. It changed his life back home, too. The reception he received and the support from the Bihar govt, including a govt job, have given him even greater motivation to succeed.None of it, he believes, would have been possible without his family’s support.“My family has always been a huge source of motivation and support. They supported me even when I was selling vegetables and driving an e-rickshaw,” said the para-lifter, who was affected by polio at the age of five. “It is difficult to put into words how much my family has done for me.”The Asian Para Games may be the immediate assignment, but Jhandu already has a bigger destination in mind. “My main target is the Paralympics. I am determined to win a Paralympic medal for India,” he said. “I am prepared to put in whatever hard work is required.”For the boy from a small village in Bihar, the journey that once seemed unimaginable has only made him dream bigger.
Article Summary: Jhandu Kumar used to sell vegetables and drive an e-rickshaw to meet his own expenses and help run the family household. Today, the Bihar para-powerlifter is a Commonwealth Games bronze medallist, has secured a government job and is preparing to represent India at Asian Para Games.

Article Title: Asian Para Games: Can India’s para-athletes script another 100-medal triumph despite a smaller contingent?
Article Text:
Archer Sheetal Devi from India prepares to fire during the Paralympic Games in Paris on Thursday, Aug. 29, 2024. (File Photo/ AP)

166 athletes across 10 disciplines: India’s medal prospects

From 14 medals to 108: India’s remarkable rise

The progression across four editions reflects the growing depth of Indian para-sports:

Paralympic success underlines India’s growing potential

Can India repeat its 100-medal achievement?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Aichi-Nagoya: Another opportunity to raise the bar

India’s para-athletes will look to build on the country’s remarkable rise in international para-sports as the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games gets underway in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, on October 18. After India’s fourth-place finish at the Asian Games 2026, the para contingent will aim to continue the country’s impressive medal-winning run at the continental event.India will be represented by 166 athletes across 10 disciplines at the October 18-24 event. The contingent features several Paralympic medallists, world champions and emerging talents, including archer Sheetal Devi, badminton stars Pramod Bhagat and Suhas Yathiraj, and para-table tennis player Bhavina Patel.India’s recent performances at the Asian Para Games and Paralympics have established the country as an increasingly competitive force in para-sports. From 14 medals at the inaugural edition in 2010 to a record 108 in Hangzhou in 2023, the progress has been remarkable. The challenge in Aichi-Nagoya will be to build on that foundation and demonstrate that the momentum can continue, even with a smaller contingent.Can India cross the 100-medal mark for the second consecutive edition? While the size of this year’s squad makes comparisons with Hangzhou particularly interesting, India’s established medal-winners and growing strength across disciplines provide reasons for optimism.India’s contingent comprises 111 male and 55 female athletes, alongside 94 team officials and support staff and 15 contingent staff members.Para-athletics accounts for the largest share, with 62 athletes, followed by para-badminton with 28 and para-swimming with 16. Para-shooting has 13 athletes, while para-archery and para-table tennis have 11 and 10, respectively. The remaining disciplines are blind football (10), para-powerlifting (eight), para-judo (seven) and para-cycling (one).The squad brings together established international performers and athletes looking to make their mark at the continental level. Sheetal, Pramod, Suhas and Bhavina are among the prominent names to watch, while para-athletics is expected to play a central role in India’s medal campaign.India’s journey at the Asian Para Games offers a compelling picture of sustained improvement. The country won 14 medals at the inaugural edition in 2010, comprising one gold, four silver and nine bronze, to finish 15th in the standings.Four years later, India retained 15th place but more than doubled its tally, winning 33 medals - three gold, 14 silver and 16 bronze.The breakthrough came in 2018, when India secured 72 medals, including 15 gold, 24 silver and 33 bronze, to climb to ninth place. At Hangzhou in 2023, the contingent took another giant leap, winning 108 medals (27 gold, 32 silver and 49 bronze) to finish fifth.India has improved its medal tally in every edition so far while also making significant gains in the standings. The jump from 72 to 108 medals between the 2018 and 2023 editions was particularly impressive, taking the country past the 100-medal mark for the first time.Aichi-Nagoya offers the next opportunity to extend that progress and build on the foundations established over the previous decade.The rise at the Asian Para Games has been accompanied by a remarkable improvement in India’s performances at the Paralympics.India finished 43rd at the Rio Paralympics in 2016 with four medals. At Tokyo 2020, the country won 19 medals - five gold, eight silver and six bronze - to finish 24th. The momentum continued at Paris 2024, where India achieved its best-ever Paralympic haul of 29 medals, including seven gold, nine silver and 13 bronze, to finish 18th.These results underline the progress made by India’s para-athletes and have helped raise expectations ahead of the Aichi-Nagoya Games.India’s record-breaking 108-medal performance at Hangzhou has naturally raised expectations ahead of the Aichi-Nagoya Games. However, the contingent this time comprises 166 athletes, compared with 309 at the previous edition.That represents a reduction of 143 athletes, or approximately 46%. The smaller squad makes a repeat of the previous tally a demanding target, but it does not diminish the significance of the opportunity before the contingent.India’s able-bodied athletes also competed with a smaller contingent at the 2026 Asian Games, with the squad size falling from 661 in Hangzhou to 495 in Aichi-Nagoya. India finished with 85 medals (21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze) after winning 106 at the previous edition.The 21-medal decline came alongside a reduction of around 25% in the number of athletes. The comparison offers an interesting reference point, although it cannot be directly applied to the para contingent because the two competitions have different event structures, athlete profiles and medal opportunities.If the relationship between contingent size and medal output at the Asian Games were used purely as a mathematical illustration, the 46% reduction in India’s para contingent could suggest a medal tally of around 68. Such a figure, however, would be only a theoretical estimate, not a reliable prediction of the outcome.A more encouraging perspective comes from India’s own history at the Asian Para Games. The country won 72 medals with 211 athletes in 2018 before improving to 108 medals with 309 athletes in 2023. Those results demonstrate that medal conversion depends on far more than the size of the contingent.The quality and competitive experience of the athletes, their event specialisations and their ability to deliver on the day will all influence India’s final tally. A smaller squad can still produce an impressive return if its members make the most of their medal opportunities.India’s fourth-place finish at the Asian Games has provided a positive backdrop for the para contingent, even though the able-bodied athletes’ final tally of 85 medals was below their Hangzhou total of 106.The Asian Para Games present a fresh opportunity for India to underline the breadth of its sporting progress. The country’s para-athletes have steadily improved their medal totals, climbed the continental standings and carried that momentum onto the Paralympic stage.The immediate target will be to produce strong performances across the 10 disciplines and make the most of the opportunities available. A second consecutive 100-medal finish would be a landmark achievement, while another strong overall showing would further consolidate India’s position among Asia’s leading para-sport nations.The numbers suggest that matching Hangzhou will be challenging, but the bigger story is the remarkable journey that has taken India from 14 medals in 2010 to 108 in 2023.
Article Summary: India will be represented by 166 athletes across 10 disciplines at the October 18-24 event. The contingent features several Paralympic medallists, world champions and emerging talents, including archer Sheetal Devi, badminton stars Pramod Bhagat and Suhas Yathiraj.

The Indian contingent brought a glimpse of the country's 5,000-year-old heritage to the opening ceremony of the Para Asian Games on Sunday, with athletes wearing ceremonial blazers featuring motifs inspired by ancient Indian civilisation.More than 100 Indian athletes took part in the ceremony, led by Paralympic medallist sprinter Simran Sharma and top shuttler Pramod Bhagat , who carried the national flag as the contingent marched with the Tricolour.The ceremonial blazers featured prints of seals from the Indus Valley, drawing on the ancient script and motifs of one of the world's oldest civilisations.“Team India walked out wearing more than just ceremonial dress -- they wore 5,000 years of civilisation. The Indian contingent’s ceremonial blazer is a tribute to our heritage,” the Paralympic Committee of India said.The blazers also featured SaptSindhu on the collar, representing the land of the seven rivers and the mighty Saraswati. The Tricolour was prominently displayed on the pocket.India has sent a 281-member contingent to the Games, comprising 168 athletes -- 112 men and 56 women -- who will compete across 11 disciplines.The Games will conclude on October 24, with around 3,000 athletes from 45 nations competing under the motto "Imagine One Heart".India had its most successful Asian Para Games campaign in Hangzhou in 2023, finishing fifth in the medal standings with a record 111 medals, including 29 gold, 31 silver and 51 bronze.

The fifth edition of the Asian Para Games will be held in Aichi-Nagoya between October 18 and 24, with 45 nations competing across 19 disciplines at the event.However, some events have already started on Friday, two days before the opening ceremony on October 18th.The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports (MYAS) has cleared 168 athletes for the upcoming 5th Asian Para Games 2026, to be held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. A total contingent of 281 members has been cleared, comprising 168 athletes, 98 team officials/supporting staff and 15 contingent staff.The contingent size is significantly smaller in this edition when compared to the previous edition held in Hangzhou, China, in 2023, where India fielded 303 athletes.The sharp drop in the contingent size is owing to the absence of disciplines such as Blind Chess, Para-Rowing and Para-Canoeing in which India had fielded athletes, as well as the strict quota restrictions by the Organising Committee in many sporting disciplines, news agency ANI reported.Of the 168 athletes, 112 are male, and 56 are female, who will compete across 11 disciplines.Over seven days of competition, around 3,000 athletes will compete across 18 sports at venues across Aichi-Nagoya and neighbouring cities in Japan.Held three years after Hangzhou 2022, the fifth edition of the Games will be staged under the motto "Imagine One Heart", celebrating unity, passion and the power of sport to bring people together.As we count down to the Opening Ceremony, here's the full schedule for Aichi-Nagoya 2026:
